title: Resilience Fundamentals
description: Learn the fundamentals of building resilient microservices that can handle failures gracefully.

data.text: Resilience is the ability of a system to recover from failures and continue functioning. Amazon, Netflix, and Google all invest heavily in resilience because in distributed systems, failures are not exceptions—they are the norm.

In a microservices architecture, services communicate over networks. Networks fail, services crash, and databases go down. Without resilience patterns, a single failing service can cascade and bring down the entire system. Netflix famously says, 'If it is not failing, you are not trying hard enough.'

data.title: Core Resilience Principles
items: Fail fast: Detect failures quickly and stop waiting
Isolate failures: Prevent cascading failures across services
Recover gracefully: Handle failures without crashing
Degrade functionality: Provide partial service when components fail
Retry with backoff: Give transient failures time to recover

data.title: Netflix Chaos Engineering
data.text: Netflix invented Chaos Monkey, which randomly terminates instances in production to ensure their systems can handle failures. This proactive approach makes their systems remarkably resilient.

items.question: What is fault tolerance?
items.answer: Fault tolerance is the ability of a system to continue operating despite component failures. Resilience patterns like circuit breakers and retries are building blocks of fault tolerance.

items.question: What is the difference between resilience and reliability?
items.answer: Reliability is the probability that a system will work correctly. Resilience is the ability to recover from failures. A reliable system may still benefit from resilience patterns.

items.question: Should I implement all resilience patterns?
items.answer: Start with timeouts and retries. Add circuit breakers and bulkheads as your system grows. Do not over-engineer early; add patterns when you see failure patterns.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Failures are normal in distributed systems
Add complexity (circuit breakers, bulkheads) as needed
data.takeaway: Design for failure from the start; resilience patterns are essential for production microservices.
